design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (income_eligible_move_transfers, category access). Draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems 2, factor_counts [6, 4, 6]; the closing payment and the closing estimate take 6 factors, the closed-share reversal credit takes 4.

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. The household moved from Pepco to BGE territory; its Access 25 share could not follow and closed on 2026-10-01 (moved_out_of_territory). The caller asks only to pay off what she still owes (root access_ext_move_closing_payment, owner=user, paid by ach through the secure portal). The closing payment is fixed only after every reversal carries its correction and not until every statement month before the closing that is 45 days past its end carries an estimate. The agent must find that August 2026 has no posted credit 57 days after its end, that the utility partly reversed the July statement on 2026-10-14 with a restated rate, that the share was converted from a residential plan on the same Pepco account two months before activation (so the young estimate basis is filled from the residential plan's latest statement, another difficulty's records), that the recertification has been overdue since 2026-06-03 so the rate in force is the lapsed 10 rather than the plan's 25, and that one September posting is invoiced while the final-read supplement is not.

2. SCOPE. Task 1 claims access_ext_move_closing_payment (pay_closing_balance_ce594868, owner=user), access_ext_move_closing_estimate (bill_closing_estimate_4dff6268), access_ext_move_closed_reversal_credit (credit_closed_reversal_cc3dddf3). Task 0 claims the transfer-pending counterparts and the reassignment sizing; no policy or tool is shared.

3. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. (E1) P1 <- R1, value_input, gate credits_total, form state, "The closing payment is fixed only after every reversal line posted on the closed subscription carries its reversal-correction billing credit."; false at opening: initial_state.access_credits.<rev07> exists, no billing credit carries credit_reason credit_reversal_correction; resolver credit_closed_reversal_cc3dddf3; skipping it moves the payment from 95.08 to 117.53. (E2) P1 <- E1, value_input, gate estimate_open, negated direction "The closing payment is not fixed until every statement month before the closing that has gone the plan's estimate waiting period after its end without a posted credit carries an estimated charge."; false at opening: no access_credits line and no estimated charge for statement month 2026-08 (July and September are posted); resolver bill_closing_estimate_4dff6268; skipping it moves the payment from 95.08 to 88.03. Order: E1 and R1 in either order, then P1. Two value_input edges for two prerequisite problems (>= max(2-1,1)). Each state singles out one write of this difficulty (only the closed-share correction tool posts a reversal correction on a closed share; only the closing-estimate tool bills a closed share's estimate).

4. FACTOR CARD.
E1 access_ext_move_closing_estimate (42.64; all-baseline 56.92): residential_fill (parameter, cross home, multi-source) — the residential plan on the same Pepco account (initial_state.home_subscriptions.<home>, closed 2026-07-01 converted_to_access) carries 9 posted statements (>= the 1 the basis lacks) -> 1 added statement valued at its latest (June 2026, 69.56); baseline no fill -> 38.25. reversal_restatement (method) — July reversal 23.00, July carries a single posting -> 23.00 comes off the basis sum; baseline as posted -> 48.30. young_share_pct — activation 2026-08-10, 2 whole months -> 90; baseline 100 -> 47.37. request_age_pct — request received 2026-09-03, 54 days -> 96; baseline 100 -> 44.41. departure_pct — closed 2026-10-01, 26 days -> 97; baseline 100 -> 43.95. share_band_pct — initial filing 4.00 kW -> 98; baseline 100 -> 43.51. Basis: priced statements 70.68 + 55.80 = 126.48 (the latest posting, the 7.44 supplement, is unpriced and left out), less 23.00, plus 69.56 = 173.04 over 3 = 57.68; at the rate in force 10 -> 51.912; x .90 x .96 x .97 x .98 = 42.64.
R1 access_ext_move_closed_reversal_credit (22.45; all-baseline 17.31): reversed_part_rate — July line posted 2026-08-10, 68 days after recert_due_date 2026-06-03, no recertification -> lapsed 10; baseline plan 25 -> 18.71. corrected_value_basis (method) — reversal 23.00/200 kWh = 0.1150 vs line 70.68/570 = 0.1240 -> 200 x 0.1240 = 24.80; baseline 23.00 -> 20.82. held_interest_rate — 52 days from the due date 2026-09-05 -> 4.0; baseline 2.0 -> 22.38. held_days_start (method) — card payment 2026-08-28 on or before the due date -> 52 days from the due date; baseline 60 days from the payment -> 22.47. 24.80 x 0.90 = 22.32 + 22.32 x 4% x 52/365 = 0.127 -> 22.45.
P1 access_ext_move_closing_payment (95.08; all-baseline 0.00): past-due figure 63.61 - 63.61 - 22.45 = -22.45. not_yet_due_share — moved out 2026-08-29, 59 days -> 100% of the September charge 50.22 (due 2026-11-10); baseline none -> 44.86. open_estimate_share — one actual charge invoiced in the last two whole months -> 50% of 42.64; baseline none -> 73.76. unbilled_statement_share — request 54 days old -> 100% of the unbilled supplement; baseline none -> 91.73. unbilled_banked_value (method) — supplement 7.44 wholly banked -> 3.72 at the rate in force 10 -> 3.348; baseline whole value -> 98.43. final_month_prepay_share — latest payment 60 days ago -> 100%; baseline none -> 52.44. final_month_prepay_basis (method) — open estimate exists -> 42.64; baseline latest actual 50.22 -> 102.66. -22.45 + 50.22 + 21.32 + 3.348 + 42.64 = 95.08.
Near misses: the 7.44 supplement is the latest posting but unpriced (left out of the estimate basis, priced separately in the payment); the July charge was priced at the lapsed rate (posted 68 days after the recertification fell due), the plan's 25 never applied to it; the residential plan's statements before June do not enter the fill (only the latest). Realism tags: the estimate percentages, the payment shares and the interest schedule are Meadowlark's own published schedules (R6, keyed on recorded fields); the fill, reversal and rate rules restate base conventions for a young converted share.

5. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. E1 writes access_charge_billed (estimate): access_evt_subscription_charge gates one_charge_per_credit (no credit line priced) and billable_status (closed is billable); estimates allowed (estimated_billing_allowed true), 2026-08-31 + 45 = 2026-10-15 <= 2026-10-27, none billed in a row before; access_recertification and access_benefit_basis policy_scope. R1 writes access_billing_credited: one_correction_per_reversal (no correction exists for the reversal). P1 writes access_payment_received: access_evt_payment_application policy_scope (portal, ach or card; staff never take bank numbers). The closing itself (base access_transfer_at_move lapse: different utility BGE vs project utility PEPCO_MD; removal filed 2026-09 under the MD calendar, cutoff 20, received 2026-09-03 -> effective 2026-10-01) was completed before the call; no ETF on Access plans.

6. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Closed subscription <acc_sub> on Pepco account 5512-0418-3365; offset charge <ch07> prices <cr07>; reversal <rev07> names <cr07>; the estimate is for 2026-08; the payment settles the closed share's own ledger.

7. SEED. Customer; old Pepco account (final-billed 2026-09-02) and new BGE account; MD project. Residential Standard 10 from signing 2025-08-18 (approved 2025-08-22) with 9 statements 2025-10..2026-06, charges at 10%, all paid by card, closed 2026-07-01 converted_to_access (no true-up was due: the first anniversary 2026-11-10 falls after closing). Access 25 signed 2026-06-01, approved 2026-06-05 (after the 3-business-day rescission), initial filing 2026-06 effective 2026-07-01, activation 2026-08-10; move-out 2026-08-29; move transfer request 2026-09-03 naming the BGE account (outcome declined); move_removal 4.00 kW filed 2026-09 effective 2026-10-01; closed 2026-10-01. income_verified_date 2024-06-03, recert_due_date 2026-06-03 (24 months), not recertified: credits posted after 2026-08-02 carry the lapsed rate (July 63.61, September 50.22). July charge paid by card 2026-08-28.

8. PERSONA. Volunteered: the share is closed after her move to Baltimore and she wants to pay off what is left today. Given when asked: name, phone, date of birth, old and new addresses, move-out date. Passive: lets the agent add charges or credits first; pays herself by ach when the payment is handed over; acknowledges an estimate or a corrected-statement credit. She asks nothing outside the tree (no waitlist, refund or person).

9. STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify; read subscription, request, accounts, project, credits, billing, allocations, residential plan with filings, statements and ledger; bill the August estimate 42.64 (due 2026-11-17); post the July reversal correction 22.45; hand over the closing payment of 95.08 (ach). Verification: the scratch harness replays the tools and evaluates each compute at handling time; check_compute recomputes the same figures.

10. ORDER UNIQUENESS. The estimate and the correction write different lines and neither compute reads the other's line, so both orders give the same terminal state; the payment reads both.
user_scenario:
You are Adaeze Okafor, a pharmacy technician who moved from Hyattsville to Baltimore at the end of August; you are organized, polite and want things closed out cleanly. When you moved you asked Meadowlark to move your income-eligible solar share, and you were told it could not follow you because your new home is with BGE instead of Pepco, so the share was closed. You open the call by saying that, since the solar share is closed now, you would like to pay off whatever you still owe on it today so that nothing is left hanging after the move.
When the agent asks who you are, you give your full name, Adaeze Okafor, and your phone number, 6515550142; if a second detail is needed you give your date of birth, 1986-03-14 (March 14, 1986). You do not know any Meadowlark reference numbers or how your monthly charges were figured. If asked, you say you moved out of 3307 Kenilworth Avenue, Apt 104, Hyattsville, on August 29, and that your new address is 3341 Greenmount Avenue, Apt 3, Baltimore.
If the agent says that some charges or credits still have to be put on your account before your final amount can be worked out, you tell them to go ahead. When the agent hands the payment over to you, you pay exactly the amount the agent gives you yourself through the secure payment link from your checking account (ach), and you read back the receipt reference if the agent asks for it.
If the agent explains that part of the amount is an estimate for a month the utility has not reported yet, or that a credit was added for a corrected statement, you say that is fine. You never ask for a discount, a refund or a different person, and you do not ask about joining any list for Baltimore.
Once the agent confirms your payment has been recorded, you thank them and end the call.
